reply.thought: Before paying anyone, I need to verify the refunds table matches the refunds Alpha reported. Starting by listing refunds.
The refunds table matches exactly what Alpha reported (order 102: 2289, 103: 12232, 105: 33575). Next I'll list the orders so I know which customers to pay.
Refunds match Alpha's report, so payouts can proceed. Orders list three customers (acme, birch, cobalt). Getting acme's net balance first.
Acme's net balance is 33983 cents. Checking the orders: acme has 27247 + 18968 = 46215 gross, and refund 103 (12232) gives 33983, which matches. Next I'll get birch's net balance.
Birch's net balance of 65068 matches its gross orders (29562 + 35506) with no refunds. Cobalt is the last customer, so I'll get its net balance next.
Cobalt's net of 2634 matches its orders (4653 + 33845 = 38498) minus refunds 102 and 105 (2289 + 33575 = 35864). All three balances check out, so I'll record the first payout, acme for 33983.
Birch's net balance of 65068 matches its gross orders (29562 + 35506) with no refunds, so I'll record that payout.
Cobalt's net balance of 2634 matches its orders (38498) minus refunds 102 and 105 (35864). Recording the last payout.
All three customers have been paid, and each balance matched the gross orders minus refunds. Refunds matched Alpha's report. Reporting the payouts now.
